第 80 章 Stop Your Team from Bikeshedding, and Saying "Bikeshedding"阻止你的团队自行车棚效应，以及说「自行车棚效应」

Ian Nowland / 伊恩·诺兰

— 第 220 页 —

The term "bikeshedding" has achieved wide usage as a way of calling out nonproductive feedback. The challenge is that the usual situations in which the term is used have ambiguity about which party is at fault. Thus, as a manager, when you hear members of your team dismiss feedback as bikeshedding, it is your responsibility to dig in and ensure that they have sought out the other parties' perspectives and communicated their reasoning. On the flipside, when your team is being accused, take it as a guide that they need to try and raise the quality of their feedback.

「自行车棚效应」一词已被广泛用作指出非生产性反馈的方式。挑战在于这个词使用的通常情境中，哪一方有错是模糊的。因此作为经理，当你听到团队成员把反馈 dismissed 为自行车棚效应时，你有责任深入挖掘并确保他们寻求了其他方的视角并沟通了他们的理由。反过来，当你的团队被指责时，把它作为他们需要尝试提高反馈质量的指南。

For those unfamiliar with the term, the best description is the email that popularized it, from Poul-Henning Kamp to a FreeBSD email list, posted at http://bikeshed.com/. What he describes is this process around a decision being critiqued: 1. Experts think deeply about all options and trade-offs and put forward a proposal. 2. The proposal is reviewed by a committee of non-experts. 3. Rather than focus on the deep trade-offs, the committee spends its time voicing objections and making counterproposals only on trivial details. This is now called bikeshedding. Within companies, the "experts" are individuals or teams that have made a decision. The "committee" comprises stakeholders who don't agree. Their bikeshedding generally takes two forms, either focusing on trivial details of the implementation that don't meet their needs or proposing a completely different solution: "why can't you just do X, instead."

对于不熟悉这个词的人，最好的描述是让它流行起来的那封邮件，来自 Poul-Henning Kamp 到 FreeBSD 邮件列表，发布在 http://bikeshed.com/。他描述的是围绕一个被批评的决策的过程：1. 专家深入思考所有选项和权衡，提出一个提案。2. 提案由非专家委员会审查。3. 委员会不聚焦深度权衡，而是花时间只在琐碎细节上表达反对和提出反提案。这现在叫自行车棚效应。在公司里，「专家」是做了决策的个人或团队。「委员会」由不同意的利益相关者组成。他们的自行车棚效应通常采取两种形式，要么聚焦不满足他们需求的实现细节，要么提出一个完全不同的解决方案：「你为什么不直接做 X 呢。」

— 第 221 页 —

Everyone bikesheds occasionally, for the reasons that we like to have our opinions heard, but do not have time to gain expert knowledge in every area that affects us. In this original formulation, it seems clear the problem is always with the bikeshedders. They are the ones making low-value noise, and so need to hold themselves to a high standard of feedback that has high utility in giving the experts reason to reconsider their decision. Therefore, it seems fine to call out their behavior when they don't. The flip side of this is that we all see decisions being made by other parties that not only affect us, but some or all of the following are also true:

每个人偶尔都会自行车棚效应，因为我们喜欢让自己的意见被听到，但没有时间在每个影响我们的领域获得专家知识。在这个原始表述中，问题似乎总在自行车棚效应者身上。他们是制造低价值噪音的人，所以需要以高反馈标准要求自己，这种反馈在给专家重新考虑决策的理由方面高效用。因此，当他们不这样做时指出他们的行为似乎没问题。另一面是我们都看到其他方做的决策不仅影响我们，而且以下部分或全部也成立：

  • We were not consulted as stakeholders in the decision我们作为决策利益相关者没有被咨询
  • The decision does not seem deeply considered决策似乎没有被深入考虑
  • The decision and its rationale were not communicated well, or at all决策及其理由没有被很好沟通，或完全没沟通

So, when we call out details of how they affect us and are told that we are bikeshedding, it is pretty frustrating to not only be heard, but to be dismissed. Now maybe what we are asking is totally wrong, but that gets to the core challenge in this situation: how much work and time should everybody be putting into decisions to make sure all stakeholders are heard, to deeply consider all possibilities and their trade-offs, and to communicate that rationale to all stakeholders in a way that they can understand on their terms? Obviously, that is an impossible standard to hold for all decisions—organizations would never get anything done. What it comes down to, then, is this is really a debate about how much time and stakeholder communication needs to go into making a decision, which is context dependent. That's what the conversation needs to be about. How do you do that, though?

所以，当我们指出它们怎么影响我们的细节却被告知我们在自行车棚效应时，不仅没被听到还被 dismiss，相当令人沮丧。也许我们问的完全是错的，但那触及了这个情况的核心挑战：每个人应该在决策上投入多少工作和时间来确保所有利益相关者被听到、深入考虑所有可能性和权衡、并以他们能按自己方式理解的方式把理由沟通给所有利益相关者？显然，这对所有决策是不可能的标准——组织永远做不成事。归结起来，这其实是关于决策需要投入多少时间和利益相关者沟通的辩论，这取决于上下文。那才是对话需要谈的。但你怎么做？

— 第 222 页 —

When your team is accusing others of bikeshedding: Coach them that when making decisions, we need to do a better job of engaging as many stakeholders as we can, ideally getting their alignment, but at minimum communicating what we are doing and why. When we don't do this, and later have stakeholders complaining, we need to understand that even when their complaints are not well founded, the fact that they are complaining means that we have missed. So be patient, explain our reasons, and maybe think about how we want to change our process for similar decisions in the future.

当你的团队指责别人自行车棚效应时：辅导他们做决策时，我们需要更好地让尽可能多的利益相关者参与，理想情况是获得他们的对齐，但至少沟通我们在做什么和为什么。当我们不这样做、后来利益相关者抱怨时，我们需要理解即使他们的抱怨没有充分根据，他们在抱怨这个事实意味着我们遗漏了。所以耐心，解释我们的理由，也许想想未来类似决策我们想怎么改变流程。

When your team is being called bikeshedders: Coach them to give the experts the benefit of the doubt that they have considered our preferred solution. Especially remember the engineering adage: "bring requirements not solutions." And like all good behaviors, this applies when we think the expert team is sloppy about how they make or communicate decisions. We never know for sure, so assume good faith, patiently ask them to explain, and if they are willing to do that, accept that they have shown enough judgment to own their decision.

当你的团队被称为自行车棚效应者时：辅导他们善意假设专家已经考虑过我们偏好的方案。尤其记住工程格言：「带需求，不带解决方案」。像所有好行为一样，这适用于当我们认为专家团队做决策或沟通决策方式草率时。我们永远不确定，所以假设善意，耐心请他们解释，如果他们愿意这样做，接受他们已经展示了足够判断来拥有自己的决策。

But more than that, remember that "bikeshedding" is negatively laden but is used in situations in which it is ambiguous who has caused the problem. Thus, it's a term best avoided.

但更重要的是，记住「自行车棚效应」是负面色彩的，但用在谁造成问题模糊的情境中。因此这个词最好避免。
